newsitem.title: FRANCE: French need freezer, less keen on dishwasher--poll.
newsitem.headline: French need freezer, less keen on dishwasher--poll.

text.p: Few French people would want to do without a freezer in their kitchen, but nearly half would be happy to live without a dishwasher, according to a poll by IPSOS for monthly magazine Cuisines et Vins de France.

The poll showed 67 percent of those interviewed said a freezer was very necessary, while 24 percent said it was fairly necessary to have one. Just nine percent said a freezer was dispensable or unnecessary.
According to the poll, which interviewed 1,012 people over age 15, the French do not rate a hi-tech kitchen very highly.
Out of nine kitchen appliances in the survey, the dishwasher came last, with 27 percent saying it was a dispensable item and 19 percent saying it was unnecessary.

Microwave ovens took seventh place, with 59 percent finding them very or fairly essential in a kitchen, while food processors were more popular, in fifth place with 65 percent saying they were very or fairly necessary.

Non-stick frying pans were the second most desirable appliance, followed by pressure cookers in third place, according to the survey. A hand-operated vegetable press was the eighth most sought-after kitchen aid.
